# Results — Study 345 (Survivorship-Bias)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One strategy — a contrarian
**"buy the past 12-month losers"** long-only book, top/bottom quintile, equal-weight,
monthly rebalanced, one execution lag — run on **two views of the same panel**: **FULL**
(every firm, including the ones that **delist** on a near-total loss) and **SURVIVORS**
(the same panel reduced to names still alive at the end, i.e. a current-membership
universe projected backwards). The gap between the two reads is the survivorship bias.
The deterministic synthetic core is the headline; a real large-cap tape is the
illustration. As-of **2026-05-31** (last full month); match the fingerprints to confirm
you hold the same tape.*

## Synthetic core — the bias as a function of how many firms die

Deterministic panel: 200 names, 240 months, **no true cross-sectional edge planted**
(`signal_strength = 0`), seed 345. The lowest-quality names are doomed: they bleed, take
a −80% delisting loss, and leave the tape. We sweep the `death_rate` and run the SAME
buy-losers book on FULL vs SURVIVORS. Synthetic panel fingerprint (death_rate 0.30):
`8d30d737ae8c`.

| death rate | view | Sharpe | mean (%/yr) | HAC *t* | Δ Sharpe (surv − full) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | FULL | +0.63 | +9.83 | +2.87 | — |
| | SURVIVORS | +0.63 | +9.83 | +2.87 | **+0.00** |
| 0.15 | FULL | +0.46 | +7.20 | +2.09 | |
| | SURVIVORS | +0.55 | +8.75 | +2.60 | **+0.10** |
| **0.30** | **FULL** | **+0.30** | **+4.87** | **+1.38** | |
| | **SURVIVORS** | **+0.60** | **+9.60** | **+2.83** | **+0.30** |
| 0.45 | FULL | +0.06 | +1.00 | +0.27 | |
| | SURVIVORS | +0.60 | +9.85 | +2.84 | **+0.54** |

- **The control passes.** At `death_rate = 0` (no firm ever delists) the FULL and
  SURVIVORS panels are identical, and so are the reads — Δ Sharpe = **+0.00**, HAC *t* =
  +2.87 on both. The harness invents no gap where there is none.
- **The bias is manufactured, not inflated, at the headline.** At `death_rate = 0.30` the
  honest FULL tape shows **no edge** (HAC *t* = **+1.38**, below 2): the buy-losers rule
  keeps stepping on the firms that go to zero. Delete those firms — the only thing the
  SURVIVORS view does — and the *same rule on the same data* prints HAC *t* = **+2.83**, a
  textbook "significant" edge. **The edge did not exist; the deletion created it.**
- **Monotone in the death rate.** The more firms die, the bigger the lie: Δ Sharpe rises
  +0.00 → +0.10 → +0.30 → +0.54 as the death rate goes 0 → 0.45, while the FULL-tape *t*
  decays to noise (+2.87 → +0.27). Survivorship bias is not a rounding error; at a
  realistic deletion rate it is the entire result.

## Real illustration — the same trap on a live large-cap tape

The convenience universe (20 current US large-caps via Yahoo total-return monthly,
2005-02 → 2026-05, 255 monthly returns) **is itself survivors-only** — it is built from
*today's* membership, so the delisted names of the last two decades (Lehman, Bear Stearns,
GM '09, the dot-com bankruptcies) are simply absent. Running the buy-losers rule here can
therefore only show the *biased upper bound*:

| Tape | Sharpe | mean (%/yr) | HAC *t* | n | Fingerprint |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| Survivors-only large-caps (current membership) | +0.78 | +17.78 | +3.52 | 255 | `ba8283a7a103` |

> **Survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** This +3.52 *t* is **not** evidence
> of a real edge — it is the *symptom* the study is about. The universe is current
> membership projected back, so every name in it survived; the rule's apparent skill is
> partly the guarantee that the losers it bought did not delist. We have no point-in-time
> tape with the dead names here, so this number is an **upper bound** and is *quoted to be
> distrusted*. The synthetic core (above), where we can toggle the dead names on and off,
> is what carries the verdict — and it shows the honest read is much weaker. The loader
> enforces `allow_survivorship_bias=True` so this caveat cannot be skipped.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** On the honest FULL tape at a realistic death rate the strategy has
  **no edge** (HAC *t* = +1.38 < 2). The only place a "significant" signal appears is the
  survivors-only view, where it is manufactured by deletion. A synthetic positive control
  never backs a Signal stamp, and the real tape we have is itself biased — so there is no
  certifiable real signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to trade: the edge that a survivors-only
  backtest advertises evaporates the instant the firms that actually died are put back.
- **Does survivorship bias manufacture/inflate an edge? — CONFIRMED.** It is real,
  directional (upward for long-biased rules that hold the recoverers and not the dead),
  and monotone in the deletion rate; at 30% deletion it turns a *t* = 1.4 non-result into
  a *t* = 2.8 "discovery", and at 0% deletion it correctly vanishes.
